edition.en: Poems of Gerard Manley Hopkins (1918), edited by Robert Bridges, from the scan-backed transcription on Wikisource; the editor’s notes omitted
edition.zh: 据维基文库依扫描本校录的《霍普金斯诗集》（1918），罗伯特·布里奇斯编；略去编者注

basis.en: Written in 1881 and first published in 1918; the author died in 1889 and the editor in 1930.
basis.zh: 1881 年写成，1918 年首次出版；作者卒于 1889 年，编者卒于 1930 年。

note.en: Written in 1881 after a visit to Inversnaid, on Loch Lomond. A brown Highland stream rushes down into the loch, and the poem ends with a plea that wild and wet places be left alone. Its dialect words, “degged” for sprinkled and “braes” for hillsides, are part of its music.
note.zh: 1881 年霍普金斯到洛蒙德湖畔的因弗斯奈德游历后写成。一条褐色的高地溪流冲进湖里，诗以一句恳求作结：让荒野与湿地保持原样。诗里的方言词，比如“degged”（沾湿）和“braes”（山坡），是它音乐的一部分。

excerpt.orig:
What would the world be, once bereft
Of wet and of wildness? Let them be left,
excerpt.en:
What would the world be, once bereft
Of wet and of wildness? Let them be left,
excerpt.zh:
这世界会成什么样，一旦失去
湿润与荒野？让它们留着吧，

note.en: A brown Highland burn rendered in dense, rushing sound, ending in an early plea for wild places; vivid and much loved, but a sketch beside his major sonnets.
note.zh: 以密集奔涌的声音写高地溪流，结尾较早地为荒野请命；鲜活可爱，比起他的重要十四行诗仍是速写。
